origins: Trauma, accidents, crime, illness, or frightening events can convince the mind that danger is everywhere. The body stays on alert, and the world feels like a minefield. We may avoid places, people, and activities to stay safe.
teaches: “He who dwells in the shelter of the Most High will abide in the shadow of the Almighty,” and the psalmist calls the LORD his refuge and fortress. “I will lie down and sleep in peace, for You alone, O LORD, make me dwell in safety.” “When you pass through the waters, I will be with you.” “The LORD will guard you from all evil; He will preserve your soul.” Scripture does not promise a life with no harm, but it promises God’s presence and ultimate safety in Him.
self_statements: I cannot protect myself or my family.
errors: Believing things are either perfectly safe or dangerous.
Feeling afraid and concluding that I am in danger.
questions: What happened that taught me danger is everywhere?
What is the actual likelihood of what I fear?
Where do I feel safe, even a little?
What does Scripture say about God’s presence in danger?
What would help my body calm down?
Who could help me, such as a counselor?
truth: I live in a world with real risks, but I am not alone. God is my refuge, and I can take wise precautions without living on alert. Healing from trauma is possible with support.
hw_truths: God is my refuge and fortress.
I can lie down and sleep in peace.
God is with me through the waters.
He guards my coming and going.
log: Each day, note one moment you felt safe and thank God.
actions: Write what sets off the alarm.
If trauma is behind this, talk with a counselor.
prayer: Lord, my body stays on guard. Be my refuge and my fortress. Teach me to rest in Your presence and to take wise steps without living in fear. Amen.
name_example: Sarah can write: “The Lord alone makes me dwell in safety.”
meta: Christian belief counseling for “I can never be safe.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
